title: Three-stage decomposition of the Tower of Hanoi
summary: Break moving n disks from A to C into three ordered subproblems: n - 1 disks A → B, the largest disk A → C, and n - 1 disks B → C.
context: The original problem f(n) moves n disks stacked from smallest on top to largest at the bottom from source rod A to destination rod C, illustrated here with five disks. Only one top disk may be moved at a time, and a larger disk may never sit on a smaller disk.

At the top level, A is the source rod, B is the auxiliary rod, and C is the destination rod; as recursion enters each subproblem, the three rods swap their source, auxiliary, and destination roles accordingly.
description: The left side summarizes moving all five disks from A to C, while the right side lists the three stages from top to bottom: first move the top n - 1 smaller disks from A to B using C; next move the largest disk from A to C as the single-disk subproblem f(1); finally move the n - 1 smaller disks from B onto the largest disk on C using A.

Both the first and third stages must still be recursively decomposed into legal single-disk moves rather than lifting a stack of smaller disks all at once. Dashed outlines mark positions before each stage and solid fills mark positions after it across the same five disks.
The table below lists for each stage the move task, auxiliary rod, and resulting disk configuration on rods A, B, and C.

frames.title: Three-stage decomposition of the Tower of Hanoi
frames.explanation: These three sequentially dependent stages imply the move-count recurrence T(n) = 2T(n - 1) + 1 (not printed in the figure). Although the first and third subproblems have the same size, they assign different source, auxiliary, and destination rods.
